Sten-Åke Elminga,⁎ , Paul Layerb, Ulf Söderlundc

ABSTRACT
ApaleomagneticandchronogicalstudyhasbeenperformedontheTuringegabbro-diabaseformationandona
crosscuttingbasicdykeincentralSwedenandontheJoulovaaragabbrointrusioninnorthernSwedeninthe
FennoscandianShield.U-Pbageofbaddeleyiteand40Ar/39Aragesofhornblendeandbiotiterevealacooling
historyofthedeepgabbro-diabaseintrusioninTuringe.Thecoolingissuggestedtohavetakenplaceintwo
stages,onerelatedtothetimeofintrusionintemperaturedowntoca500°Cwithacoolingrateupto46–59°/Ma
andanotheratalowerrateofca2.9°C/Ma,whichissuggestedtoberelatedwithuplift.Fromthiscooling
historyitcanbeconcludedthatthemagnetizationageofthediabase,ca1695–1700Ma,isclosetothecrys-
tallizationageandthe40Ar/39Arageofhornblende.Applyingasimilarcoolinghistoryfortheotherstudieddeep
intrusion,theca1800MagabbroofJoulovaaragabbro,itisestimatedthatthemagnetizationageofthegabbro
shouldbeclosetothatoftheU-Pbageoftheformation,althoughthepoleoftheJoulovaaragabbroisless
reliable.
ThecoolinghistorypresentedherefortheTuringegabbro-diabasehasimplicationsforestimationsofmag-
netizationagesalsoforotherdeepintrusions.
Thenewpole(Plat.=51.6°,Plon.=220.2°;A95=4.8°)oftheTuringegabbro-diabasepassesmostofthe
reliabilitycriteriaandisconsideredanewkeypoleforFennoscandia.
TheBasicdykethatcutstheTuringegabbro-diabasewasheredatedatca1200Ma(wholerock,40Ar/39Ar)
and the virtual geomagnetic pole calculated from its primary magnetization falls into the expected trend of
APWPforBaltica.
ThenewTuringekeypoleprolong thetimeof overlappingpolesforFennoscandia, indicating onlysmall
movementsoftheshieldbetweenca.1870to1700Ma.

4.2. Geochronology
In one sample from the Turinge gabbro-diabase at site 3 both
hornblendeandbiotiteweredatedbythe40Ar/39Armethod.Asingle
hornblende run gives a well-defined plateau with an age of
1703 ± 6Ma. A second run resulted in a slightly lower age
(1687 ± 13Ma),buttheplateauismorescattered,possiblyreflecting
alteration(Fig.8;Table2).Alsothedatingofbiotiterevealplateauages
inthetworuns,bothageslowerthanthoseofhornblende.Thebiotite
plateau ages of the two runs are different from each other
(1622 ± 5Ma and 1645 ± 4Ma; Fig. 8), possibly related to differ-
ences in grain size, the larger grain is older than the smaller one. A
biotitegrainfromthegabbro-diabase atsite2 wasalsodated, witha
well-defined plateau age of 1627 ± 11Ma. This results in a mean

6. Summaryandconclusion
TheU-Pbageofbaddeleyite(1700 ± 4Ma)and40Ar/39Aragesof
hornblende (1703 ± 6, 1687 ± 13Ma) and biotite (1622 ± 5;
1645 ± 4; 1627 ± 11Ma) reveal a cooling history of the gabbro-
diabaseatTuringe.Thecoolingissuggestedtohavetakenplaceintwo
stages with different cooling rates, one with an estimated rate up to
46–59°/Ma,relatedtothetimeofintrusionandanother,moreslow,ca
Fig.10.ConcordiaplotofU-PbdatafrombaddeleyiteintheTuringegabbro- 2.9°C/Ma, related to uplift. From this cooling history it can be con-
diabase.Ellipsesindicateerroratthe95%confidencelevel.
cludedthattheestimatedmagnetizationageofthegabbro-diabase,ca
1690–1700Ma, is close to that of the crystallization age and the
40Ar/39Arhornblendeage.ThissmalltimedifferencebetweentheU-Pb
age andage ofmagnetization isdifferentfrom theca80Ma thatwas
estimated for the 1786Ma Hoting gabbro. Based on a supposed fast
initial cooling similar to that disclosed from the Turinge gabbro-dia-
base,themagnetizationageoftheHotinggabbroisnowsuggestedtobe
close to 1780Ma. This has implications for estimations of magnetiza-
tionagesalsoforotherdeepintrusions.
ThenewpaleomagneticpoleoftheTuringegabbro-diabasefulfills
mostofthecriteriaforareliablepoleandisconsideredakeypolefor
Fennoscandia.Thispoleprolongthetimespanofoverlappingpolesfor
Fennoscandia/Baltica indicating only small movements of the shield
betweenca1870and1700Ma.TheJoulovaarapoleisnotveryreliable,
but plots close to other ca 1800Ma poles of Fennoscandia. The Basic
dyke that cuts the Turinge gabbro-diabase was dated at ca 1200Ma
(whole rock, 40Ar/39Ar) and the virtual geomagnetic pole calculated
fromitsprimarymagnetizationfallsintotheexpectedtrendofAPWP
